title: Greenpill Q1 2025: Laying the Groundwork
dek: Greenpill's first-quarter update for 2025 covers two new chapters, a busy ETHDenver, the General Forum on Ethereum Localism and community-led Gitcoin rounds.
excerpt: New chapters in Cape Town and London, Ontario, service projects in Denver, and a shared impact standard for Regen Coordination.
body:
Greenpill published its Q1 2025 update on Paragraph on April 30, 2025. The network started the year slowly, postponing its January gathering, and then centered its attention on Izzy Initiatives, a Gardens signaling pool created to carry on the legacy of Izzy.

## New chapters

Greenpill welcomed its first new chapters since revamping its onboarding: Cape Town, which holds weekly gatherings in Muizenberg, and London, Ontario, led by the Institute for Community Sustainability, whose work includes a Repair Café program and a Thing Library. Both chapters were trained on Charmverse, Karma GAP and Safe multisig wallets.

## ETHDenver and Ethereum Localism

In February, Greenpill members gathered in Denver for the second time. Fourteen people stayed at a Greenpill hackerhouse, and a Friday barbecue brought in friends from across the regen space. Ryan organized three service projects under the name Greenpill Goonies Giveback: two shifts at Food Bank of the Rockies and a river cleanup with the Greenway Foundation that pulled 17 pounds of litter from the South Platte River. Many members also attended the General Forum on Ethereum Localism in Boulder.

## Regen Coordination and local rounds

Regen Coordination began using the Common Impact Data Standard (CIDS) to measure project activity and outcomes, with onboarding workshops in English, Portuguese and Spanish. Community-led Gitcoin rounds included Regen Rio from Greenpill Brasil, a Web3 Universities round for African universities, a DeSci community round and a Gardens round where members proposed and voted on treasury allocations. Greenpill Toronto hosted the first Chapter Demo Day on April 21.
